one_liner: Pre-alpha strict-only JavaScript and WebAssembly engine in Zig whose interpreter beats QuickJS-NG on its author's micro-benchmarks.
what_it_does: Cynic is a from-scratch ECMAScript engine (plus a WebAssembly interpreter called Sarcasm) written in Zig, shipped as a `cynic` CLI (lex, parse, eval, run, repl) and a Zig embedding API built around an explicit `Engine` struct with allocator threading and no globals. It is strict-only (no sloppy mode, no Annex B, no legacy web-compat built-ins) and starts each realm hardened: frozen primordials, built-in `harden()`, and `eval`/`Function` off unless the host passes `--allow=eval`. It is not API-compatible with QuickJS; the README says the embedding API and runtime behavior are still evolving.
how_it_is_fast: The bytecode is register-file plus implicit accumulator (Ignition/Hermes style) with one-byte opcodes, narrow immediate forms, fused opcodes such as `make_array_n` and `LoopIncLt`, a post-finalization `Star r; Ldar r` forwarding pass, and a direct-threaded dispatch loop in the Lantern interpreter; the docs reject QuickJS's pure-stack design for its higher dispatch count. Values are NaN-boxed with the JSC encoding (unboxed doubles, 16-bit tags), and load, store, computed-property and method-call sites carry typed inline caches (the benchmarking doc credits the `lda_property` IC with a 66% drop on prop_access). Above Lantern sit two JIT tiers, Bistromath (T1) and Ohaimark (T2), on x86_64 and AArch64, but the cross-engine numbers that beat QuickJS-NG were taken with `--no-jit`.
when_to_use: You embed JavaScript in a Zig program, or want a hardened-by-default JS sandbox (frozen primordials, host-gated eval and Wasm compilation) and your scripts are strict-mode or ES modules.

Interpreter-only throughput on tight int32 arithmetic, array-literal and constructor loops matters: in the author's interpreter-tier snapshot Cynic --no-jit is 3.1-6.5x faster than QuickJS-NG on arith_loop, mod_loop, array_literal_loop, construct_loop and class_instantiate.

Compute-heavy scripts of the Octane kind where QuickJS-NG is your current engine and a few MB more RSS is acceptable (crypto 1.73x, splay 1.71x, navier-stokes 1.24x, raytrace 1.21x faster in the same snapshot, derived from page data).
You need JS and WebAssembly in one small native engine on x86_64 Linux or Apple Silicon macOS.
when_not_to_use: Production use of any kind: the README calls it pre-alpha, the embedding API is still changing, test262 coverage is about 89% of the runtime-mode sweep, and closed issues include panics on large Numbers (#22, #23) and a CLI `eval` that ran code with syntax errors (#137).
Legacy or web-compat code: sloppy-mode scripts, Annex B features, `with`, legacy octal literals and Annex B regex leniencies are rejected, so a lot of npm-era code will not run unmodified.
Memory-constrained hosts: QuickJS-NG peaks at 1,792 KiB on nearly every micro fixture against 6,016-27,520 KiB for Cynic, and on deltablue 1,920 KiB vs 12,544 KiB.

Workloads like deltablue (Cynic 430 ms vs qjs 344 ms) or richards (a tie), and anything where Hermes, V8 --jitless or JSC with JIT off is an option: all three beat Cynic on every Octane macro in the same snapshot.
Windows, mobile, or a C/C++ host that needs a stable C API: Windows and mobile are unsupported and no C API is documented.

integration.form: Zig source build (`zig build`): CLI binary plus a Zig embedding API; no tagged releases
integration.dependencies: none declared in build.zig.zon; vendored test262, Wasm testsuite, Unicode, CLDR and IANA tzdata assets (Intl is a compile-time choice: -Dintl=off|stub|full)
integration.min_toolchain: Zig development build 0.17.0-dev.1275+59a628c6d, pinned in build.zig.zon (anyzig can fetch it)
integration.platforms: Native CI on x86_64-linux-gnu and Apple Silicon macOS; cross-builds aarch64-linux-gnu, x86_64-linux-musl, aarch64-macos; wasm32-freestanding for the browser playground; JIT tiers only on x86_64 and AArch64 macOS/Linux; no Windows or mobile
integration.thread_safety: not documented (state is owned by an explicit Engine struct, no globals)

gotchas: The measured posture is not the default posture: bench-cross.sh runs Cynic with --no-jit --unhardened --allow=eval, while the CLI default is hardened with both JIT tiers on; in the same snapshot the default JIT-on run is slower than --no-jit on several micros (arith_loop 99 vs 77 ms, construct_loop 337 vs 312, mod_loop 69 vs 60) and within 3% on every macro.

Harness gap: bench-cross.sh sends every engine's stdout to /dev/null and checks only the exit code, so the checksums the micro fixtures print are never compared across engines (the Octane macros do self-check, e.g. crypto throws if decryption does not round-trip). Timing is spawn-to-exit wall clock with `date +%s%3N`, so start-up is inside every number, and arith_loop, array_literal_loop, construct_loop and json_stringify keep their accumulator in a top-level script `let`, so they also time each engine's global-binding access path.

The baseline binary is pinned down after all: jsvu's QuickJS installer downloads quickjs-ng's release asset qjs-linux-x86_64, which quickjs-ng's release.yml builds on Alpine (musl) with GCC as a static CLI with static mimalloc in CMake's default Release mode; the CPU model of the benchmark host is still unstated.

The snapshot is from revision 6e125807 (2026-08-06) and covers 19 micro fixtures; bench/micros now holds 39 (BigInt, relational and double-increment fixtures added later) with no newer cross-engine snapshot. The record's note that Cynic vendors QuickJS's libregexp comes from a bench-cross.sh comment that looks stale: vendor/ has no libregexp and ARCHITECTURE.md names Perlex as Cynic's own regex engine.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Cynic over QuickJS when you want a hardened, strict-only engine with a faster interpreter on arithmetic and allocation loops and can live with pre-alpha status and 3-7x the RSS; QuickJS remains the choice for small footprint, sloppy-mode compatibility and a stable C API. Hermes (faster than Cynic on every Octane macro here) or PrimJS and Escargot are better picks when you need a mature non-JIT engine today.
verified_claims_summary: The author's internal cross-engine snapshot (tools/bench-cross.sh, revision 6e125807, Linux 6.8 x86_64, CPU model not stated, pinned to CPU 1, median of 12 subprocess wall-clock runs after one warmup) has Cynic --no-jit, built with zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast, ahead of QuickJS-NG 0.15.1 (jsvu's static musl/mimalloc release binary) on all 18 micro fixtures qjs completes (3.1-6.5x on the arithmetic and allocation loops, near ties on promise_chain and shallow_cons_miss) and on four of six Octane macros (1.2-1.7x), tied on richards and 1.25x slower on deltablue (derived from page data). The page labels itself an unpublished internal regression compass, so this is first-party evidence.
status_note: Very active (2,558 commits, last commit 2026-10-05, 26 stars, no releases) and MIT-licensed, but pre-alpha with an evolving embedding API and a pinned Zig development compiler, so treat it as an engine to watch or experiment with, not one to ship.
